summary: Independently reviewed the immutable single-commit range 9de80e2..60087e0 (HEAD verified, worktree clean before and after). The change adds schema-validated command publication for bloodbank.agent.invocation.start: the canonical schema now pins type/kind/subject/dataschema/schemaref consts and requires non-blank prompt and target; the publisher builds the complete command envelope (command_id, target+command-scoped idempotency_key per docs/event-naming.md §11.2, delivery=single_consumer, root correlation=command_id, causation null) and AJV-validates it against the generated canonical schema before any NATS connection; registry resolution is fail-closed (exact canonical-slug keys, schema_version===1, exactly one eligible fleet-scope self-referencing target) and never emits profile names; reserved extension keys cannot override canonical fields; event mode is behavior-identical to base (same envelope, subject, ordering_key, and output key set, verified by diff and test). All five required gates re-run independently with exit 0: npm test 52/52, smoketest:schemas PASS, smoketest:command live round-trip PASS, hermes-gateway pytest 62 passed, codegen regenerates eventSchemas.ts byte-identically with a clean git status. Two minor findings (YAML parse-error source-snippet echo in the route-resolution error wrapper; ajv 8.17.1 sits in the affected range of a moderate $data-only ReDoS advisory that is not reachable in this usage); neither blocks the gate.

findings.title: YAML parse errors echo registry source lines into n8n error surfaces
findings.description: The route-resolution catch wraps (error as Error).message verbatim. Verified empirically that the yaml package's parse-error messages embed the offending source line with a caret (e.g. a malformed 'profile_name: <value>: oops' line is reproduced in full). That message propagates via NodeOperationError to n8n execution error output and, when continueOnFail is enabled, into the item's json.error field, where downstream nodes could forward it onto the bus.
findings.impact: A malformed agents-registry.yaml can leak the broken line's content — potentially a profile name that registry.ts:15-17 documents as never leaving the boundary — into workflow-visible error data. Likelihood is low (requires a syntactically broken operator-managed file) and exposure is bounded to roughly one line, but it contradicts the stated non-exposure invariant.
findings.required_fix: In the catch at Bloodbank.node.ts:290-296, sanitize parser errors before wrapping: for YAMLParseError use only the reason and position (e.g. message up to the first newline, or linePos-derived 'at line X, column Y') and never the source snippet; add a publisher-node test asserting a malformed registry with a profile-name line produces an error message that does not contain that line's content.

findings.title: Introduced ajv 8.17.1 is inside the affected range of advisory GHSA-2g4f-4pwh-qvx6
findings.description: npm audit --omit=dev reports one moderate production advisory introduced by this range: ajv ReDoS when using the $data option (fixed in 8.20.0). The vulnerable condition is not present here — src/nats.ts:95 constructs Ajv2020 without $data and every validated schema is a first-party document committed under schemas/ and embedded by codegen, so no attacker-controlled schema or $data reference can reach the compiler.
findings.impact: No exploitable path in this usage; the residual risk is future code enabling $data or validating untrusted schemas against this pinned version, and audit noise gating other dependency work.
findings.required_fix: Bump the ajv pin to ^8.20.0 (or the latest 8.x) and regenerate package-lock.json via npm install ajv@^8.20.0 in a follow-up; no code change is required.
